dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: What a pretty bracelet! What a pretty vase! Goods from Liyue sure are pretty!

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: ...Uh, wait, no. These simplistic terminologies will simply not do for a novelist like me.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should purchase one of these ingeniously-made porcelain trinkets and use it as reference material for my next novel...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Mm, yes, yes! That's what we'll write.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: "The key to the turnaround was a Vision concealed within the vase!"

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Yes, that could be quite interesting indeed! What do you think, Kama?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Lady Sumida, I don't really...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: I feel that any descriptions of this vase should be well-controlled. If you spend too much time on it, the foreshadowing will become quite apparent. But at the same time, mentioning it too little will make that development seem abrupt.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Hmm, you do have a point indeed! Let me write this down...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Wait, no, let's do that somewhere else.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Also, haven't I told you a thousand times before not to call me "Lady"?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: ...But then again, having one of a pair of seemingly ordinary travelers call the other "Lady" or "Lord" isn't that uncommon a plot development either, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: "The world is vast and infinite..."

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Is that a quote from "Joururi Kidoutai"?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: That's right. Your memory's pretty sharp, Kama.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: It was a story you told me, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Phew— That felt good—

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Or should I say "this is how the largest library in the north should be"? To think that I'd have the opportunity to finish the whole Vera's Melancholy series in one go! Ah, that was wonderful!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Lady Sumida, it might be best to keep your voice down.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Ah, right. Sorry. I was getting too excited there...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: No, I'm worried that you might get hurt. That librarian has an immense aura around her...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Eh? Really? I thought she was a rather typical, slightly-lazy witch.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, but now that you mention it, these characters do tend to be the strongest. Um, right then, best not to get on her bad side...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Actually, I could write a story based on just such a character, couldn't I? Something like "The Mage of the Great Library"...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How have your travels been going?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Ah. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: #Oh ho, if it isn't the legendary {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Our travels? ...Hmm, you know, I used to go out to travel to collect reference material a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: I went to Musoujin Gorge to study how to write thunderstorms, headed to the Serpent's Head to learn how to describe a snake demon, I got Kama to join the military to better understand the lives of the Absconders...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Man, being Kama's a tough job.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: It wasn't much.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: But this on the other hand is a real journey. One with no real objective in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Only now have I discovered that there are just so many interesting things worth writing about in this world, just like in Kino's Travels.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Kama and I visited the recommended sights and stores around these parts before camping out in the wild, exchanging stories with unfamiliar travelers by the campfire...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: ...And when we woke up, we found our belongings all missing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Wait. So did that turn out okay in the end?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: It did. Honestly, when we found out that the gang of thieves had ten or more members, I thought we weren't getting our stuff back.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: But somehow, Kama was able to convince them to return our things. They even gave him these coins with raven insignias on them to go!

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Shame... I thought that this would make for an interesting story, but Kama wouldn't tell me how it all went down.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I simply did as I should. You need not worry, Lady Sumida.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: With you by my side, I doubt we'd have any trouble, even if our adventures took us to the edge of the world itself!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Speaking of which, you really have changed a lot since the whole incident with Tsurumi Island. There are things you want to do now, and opinions and doubts you want to express...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Well, if you do not find it suitable, Lady Sumida...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: No, no, I think it's great! Your views are all well-worth considering.

choices.text: Well, I'll leave the two of you alone then.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #Indeed. See you, {NICKNAME}. Let's meet at the end of all things, just like in "Flowers for Princess Fischl."

choices.text: Perhaps we'll meet again in some other place.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Lady Sumida, do you have any plans as to where we should go next?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Hmm... Now I've heard that Mondstadt is home to a very large library...
